review.summary: Round 10 reviews the whole TASK-069A branch at the round-9 fix commit. All five round-9 findings are verified fixed: the accidental numbered list, the step-decides-status wording in AI.md and the concept, the consolidated first-step error list with nothing lost, the corrected statement of what the redirect host proves with loopback wording in TASK-069L, and TASK-069F's PostgreSQL case as an acceptance criterion. A CommonMark render confirms the list structure. Scope is still documentation-only. likec4@1.60.0 validate passes and the committed PNGs are byte-identical to a fresh export with the README command; relative links and anchors resolve; the review records validate. Three new findings, one low and two info: the consent-page specification in ADR-015 missing the loopback wording, two wrapping nits, and a speculative wording point about the source of apply_in_progress.

findings.summary: ADR-015's consent-page specification does not require the loopback wording that its new limitation paragraph relies on.
findings.rationale: The new paragraph says the consent page states the loopback limitation, and TASK-069L shows that wording instead of the host for loopback redirects, but ADR-015's consent bullet and the client-name paragraph still say only that the host is shown. TASK-069E's consent API returns the host without a defined format, and an IPv6 loopback host may be returned without brackets.
findings.recommendation: Add the loopback wording to ADR-015's consent bullet and align the client-name paragraph, and optionally have TASK-069E return the host in URL form or an explicit loopback flag.

findings.summary: Two lines from the last fix are wrapped inconsistently.
findings.rationale: One TASK-069E prose line is over 80 characters and an AI.md sentence breaks early; rendering is unaffected.

findings.summary: Speculative: apply_in_progress is attributed only to a concurrent apply, although grant cleanup can also lock change-set rows.
findings.rationale: Setting a change set's grant reference to null during cleanup locks that row, so a lock-not-available error could come from cleanup and the UI would still say another apply is running.
findings.recommendation: Optionally say another transaction, for example a concurrent apply, or accept as is.

prior_finding_dispositions.rationale: The lock timeout bullet was moved and rewrapped so no continuation line starts a list, and a CommonMark render shows the intended list structure with no stray numbered list.
AI.md and the concept now say the step alone decides whether the status changes, matching ADR-015 and TASK-069I, K and M.
ADR-015 now calls the 503 case any other unexpected error and merges the duplicated bullets into one list of the first-step errors, with nothing lost from the previous text.

ADR-015 now says the server verifies the redirect URI against the allowlist and the consent page only displays the host, that a vendor callback identifies the vendor while loopback hosts identify no client, and accepts that limitation; TASK-069L adds loopback wording with a test, and its right-to-left name test was correctly removed. A remaining consent-specification gap is recorded as a new finding.
TASK-069F's PostgreSQL wait case is now an acceptance criterion with its command and CI note, and TASK-069E's lock test is limited to a raw grant insert and authorize against cleanup.
